findings.title: the P1-B fix cannot observe the failure it was built for, and the gap it documents never existed: latchSystemHalt runs inside isolateItem, which never rethrows and already Sentry-captures the failure, so the new catch in runSolicitationReleaseCycle sees nothing of that class
findings.reason: The finding is correct and the P1-B fix has been REVERTED IN FULL on the owner's decision. Verified independently before acting: recordItemFailure (release-phases.ts) already calls Sentry.captureException, guarded, with a log fallback, under tags subsystem 'solicitation-release', and isolateItem never rethrows — so the alert path existed one layer below the poller and the new capture could never observe that failure class. Two further defects the finding names were also confirmed: the fix wrote 'solicitation_release' against four existing 'solicitation-release' sites, splitting one subsystem across two tag spellings; and send_window_elapsed maps to null in BATCH_HALTED_REFUSAL_CATEGORIES, so one of the two arms cited writes no Refusal at all. SolicitationReleasePoller.ts and its test are restored to their fork-point blobs, the promised title is removed from tests_to_add, and the two poller paths are removed from allowed_edit_surface. The amendment counter is NOT decremented: surfaceAmendments stays at 2, so this branch spent its last amendment on a change that should never have landed, and the deviations file records that rather than resetting it.

findings.title: the newly emitted subsystem:'solicitation_release' Sentry signal has no bullet and no rule row in docs/runbooks/beta-launch-alerting.md, while the #1009 precedent it names added both; it also splits the lane's established subsystem:'solicitation-release' tag value
findings.reason: Resolved by the RT2-1 revert rather than by editing the runbook. The signal this finding is about no longer exists: the subsystem 'solicitation_release' capture was removed with the rest of the P1-B fix, so there is no new signal needing a bullet or a rule row, and the tag-value split it identified is gone with it. The runbook stays off allowed_edit_surface and untouched, which is the correct outcome — the finding's premise was the fix, and the fix is withdrawn.

findings.title: the new ordering case leaves closeBatchIfSettled's position unpinned: hoisting it to the top of commitWithhold (so a batch whose last row is a withhold never closes) survives both this case and the sibling batch-closure case
findings.arbiter_reasoning: A5 is neither equivalent nor on an unexecuted branch — closeBatchIfSettled runs on this exact path and the reorder changes real behaviour. It is nevertheless NOT semantically meaningful for the tested behaviour, which is the ledger write's position relative to five named writes plus last-of-all: all five relative orders and ledgerIndex === queries.length - 1 still hold under A5. Reclassified from P0-candidate to a recorded P2.

findings.reason: The signal half is factually false at both e9a6a50b and 426ccf77: src/lib/solicitation/release-phases.ts:96-107 (recordItemFailure) already raised a Sentry issue for exactly this failure, and release-phases.ts:69-81 (isolateItem) contains the throw before runSolicitationReleaseCycle can see it — see release.ts:791 and the repo's own release.integration.test.ts:2162-2163. Superseded by RT2-1; the surviving rule-row half is carried forward as RT2-2. Must be listed in the PR description's "Red-team findings rejected" section.

findings.title: vocabulary.ts's header is FALSE at HEAD as a direct result of this diff: it still says five exported lane maps have no production caller, and three of the five now have one
findings.reason: OWNER-AUTHORIZED DEFERRAL, recorded rather than fixed. The finding is accepted as true: three of the five maps gain a production caller on this branch, so the header sentence is false at HEAD. It cannot be fixed on ANY of the three swarm branches — src/lib/refusals/vocabulary.ts is outside all three edit surfaces by construction, because disjoint surfaces are the premise of running them in parallel, and #1010 has spent both amendments. #1010's own D3 proposed handing it to whichever of #1011/#1012 lands last; that does not work for the same reason. Carried on the orchestrator as a post-merge documentation sweep together with three sibling staleness findings (env-vars.md, eservices-variables.md and beta-launch-alerting.md all attribute the kill switch to writeRefusalEvent alone) under one true sentence: the ledger now has two writers and its maps have callers. Owner authorized the deferral explicitly on 2026-08-31.
